title: Finite coefficient and site extension on bounded flat input models
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (one admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings), let $\ell$ be a prime, and let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$. Use ordinary constant-ring module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Let $a\le b$ be integers and let $L\in D^b(X_{\rm et},A)$ have constructible cohomology and Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, meaning that $L\otimes^L_A H[0]$ has cohomology only in $[a,b]$ for every etale module sheaf $H$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Write $N_X=\nu_X^*$ for exact site comparison and $L_B=L\otimes^L_A B$ [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor].
There is a flat constructible complex $P$, zero outside $[a,b]$, representing $L$. It is K-flat (tensoring it with any acyclic complex is acyclic). The complexes $P\otimes_A B$, $N_XP$, and $(N_XP)\otimes_A B$ are K-flat with flat terms and vanish outside $[a,b]$; they represent respectively $L_B$, $N_XL$, and $(N_XL)_B$. The canonical tensor comparison identifies the last complex with $N_X(P\otimes_A B)$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Both $L_B$ and $N_XL$ are bounded constructible of Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ on their respective sites, as is $(N_XL)_B$ [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. No flatness or finite projective dimension of $B$ over $A$ is required. Flatness and K-flatness use [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Schemes and Noetherian rings use [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible] with $\Lambda=A$, $K=L$ and the given integers $a\leq b$. Its hypotheses are exactly that $A$ is finite, $X$ is Noetherian, and $L$ is bounded constructible with Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. It supplies a complex $P$ whose terms are flat constructible $A_X$-module sheaves, with $P^q=0$ outside $[a,b]$, and an isomorphism $L\simeq P$ in the derived category. This chooses the one input model used throughout the proof.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-bounded-flat-coefficient-site-square] to this $P$, the given $A\to B$ and $[a,b]$. Its hypotheses are the flat terms and strict bounds supplied in Step 1; it needs neither Noetherianity nor constructibility. It makes $P$, $P\otimes_A B$, $N_AP$ and $(N_AP)\otimes_A B$ K-flat with flat terms and these same bounds. Substitute the isomorphism $Q(P)\simeq L$ in its three derived representative isomorphisms to obtain exactly $L_B$, $N_AL$ and $(N_AL)_B$. Its $B_X$-linear chain comparison identifies the last complex with $N_B(P\otimes_A B)$ and localizes to the specified canonical derived comparison. Its universal Tor assertion gives Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ for the three target objects on their own sites.

These are inputs, not a single source statement of the combined assertion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-constructible-coefficient-site-square] with $C=P$. The given finite affine Noetherian cover verifies its scheme hypothesis, and Step 1 supplies its bounded termwise constructible input. Its four localized complexes have constructible cohomology in $[a,b]$. By the representative isomorphisms of Step 2 these are $L$, $L_B$, $N_AL$ and $(N_AL)_B$, the last using the canonical comparison with $N_B(P\otimes_A B)$. This proves the required bounded constructibility on both sites. Combined with Step 2 it proves every asserted property; neither new lemma assumes the coefficient map flat or of finite projective dimension.
